# r4.0-pre.10

## Synchronization upload performance

- Use a WinSCP-style directory checklist for initial and watched synchronization, with bounded preparation of the next eligible small file while the current transfer is awaiting acknowledgement.
- Reuse short-lived local parent checks within the same operation; check the actual source file when it is opened for transfer. Stop and failure paths settle the current request before proceeding, and discard unused preparation.
- Compare whole-second modification times with a two-second tolerance and size. When a corresponding local file exists, remote-newer files are retained. Files with equal size and timestamps within that tolerance can be skipped, including same-size edits during watching.
- With deletion synchronization enabled, refresh the remote listing for deletion decisions instead of relying on the previous upload-receipt protocol. Remote entries absent locally can be deleted, including remote-side additions or changes since an earlier scan.

## Included earlier fixes

This release also includes the prepared pre.9 fixes for initial passphrase focus in a new connection tab and stale error badges after synchronization restart. The pre.9 publication run was cancelled before release.

## Transfer behavior

Files smaller than 100 KiB are written directly to their destination, so partial contents can be visible while uploading. After a write failure or cancellation, removal is attempted once closing the file has succeeded. If closing or removal cannot be confirmed, partial bytes may remain; a timestamp failure can also leave uploaded bytes. Previously overwritten contents cannot be restored. Larger files use staged transfer and final rename. Partial uploads from previous attempts are not reused as complete files.

These changes bring comparison, transfer and deletion behavior closer to WinSCP. They do not promise identical behavior for every server or simultaneous edit. Review the selected local/remote folders and deletion option before starting synchronization.

## Validation and measurement limits

Generated localhost tests covered new and existing files, large files, deletion, watching, cancellation, failures and restart. A release-optimized QA GUI experiment with 4,000 new 512-byte files observed approximately 9.85 seconds with deletion enabled, measured from the final synchronization confirmation to the caught-up display. The contemporaneous WinSCP GUI observation was approximately 10.95–12.21 seconds, with a less precise completion boundary. Each application had only two runs per mode; these values do not establish general speed superiority. Empty targets contained no files to delete. Real-server performance, large-file throughput and other DPI configurations were not established by this comparison.

This is a prerelease. The stable Latest release remains r3.6. Installation is manual; this release does not automatically change existing synchronization settings.
